summary: The sole attestation confirms inherited I.1 covering with ruḥux as a self-directed object. It is already quoted; a thin cell does not justify duplicating the same source.
Keep stem I and the given mbamxalle/mbamxər pair. The m-prefixed loan formation does not establish a second stem or a new causative meaning.

The Turoyo explicitly says ruḥux, while the German identifies the covered part as the face. This contextual body-part interpretation does not justify replacing the reflexive object in the gloss or creating a face-covering sense.
gd- Infectum has directive/necessity force in the advice, coordinated with a prohibition on greeting. That discourse force is not a new form box or lexical sense.
No independent light verb plus noun idiom is established. Existing wording, including the inherited gloss spelling, is retained.
Does the verb with ruḥo regularly specify covering the face, or is that restriction supplied by this scene? The one token cannot decide.
Confirm the historical segmentation of the inherited loan formation if the editors revisit the Arabic xmr etymology; this occurrence alone does not supply it.
Remove the misspelled repeated gloss bedeicken
rationale: Bedeicken is a misspelling of the preceding bedecken. Retain one correctly spelled gloss. Both the entry example and the translation of 107/35 explicitly illustrate bedecken.
